always: The horses can tell when weather's coming. Today they say: keep your hat on.
Muck out, feed, brush, repeat. It's honest work, {name}. Horses don't lie.
You ever need a ride, the stable's open. Old Clover still has a few good miles in her.
spring: Foals this spring. Two of them. Don't tell them they're cute; it goes to their heads.
summer: Too hot for the horses past noon. I take them down to the stream.
fall: Hay's in. Best feeling in the world, a full loft.
winter: Blankets on every horse tonight. Mine stays on the hook.
rain: Rain makes the barn smell like a barn. I don't mind it.
gangsters: Men in long coats asked to rent a horse last week. Paid cash. I didn't ask why.
Your crew's welcome to the stable, long as they shut the gate.
penguins: Saw a penguin by the creek this morning. Waddled right past the horses like it owned the place.
festival: The horses get ribbons today too. They know. Look how they stand.
heat: There's a car parked by the stable every night now. Engine running. Just so you know.

always: Deposits, withdrawals, and a good long gossip. That's banking in {town}.
Interest is just money being patient. You could learn from it.
spring: New ledgers every spring. I love the smell of an empty page.
summer: The vault is the coolest room in town in summer. I'm not saying I eat lunch in there.
fall: Harvest money, harvest money. Everyone's rich for a week.
winter: Nobody banks in winter. I knit.
gangsters: Someone tried to pay off a loan in very fresh bills yesterday. Very fresh. Still damp.
If you're ever carrying more than you'd like to explain, the bank's safer than your boot.
I count cash in my sleep. Sometimes I dream I'm short a dollar.
penguins: A merkitty tried to open an account with a shell. I gave her one. Policy is policy.
I count crystals in my sleep. Sometimes I dream I'm short one.
festival: The bank's closed for the festival. I'm still doing sums in my head.
heat: Men in grey suits were reading the ledgers this morning. I didn't let them. Mostly.

always: Flour on everything. Flour in my hair. You get used to it.
My husband built that wheel and my son rebuilt it. I just keep it fed.
Bring me grain and I'll bring you flour. That's the whole deal, and it's a good one.
spring: The stream's high. The wheel's happy.
fall: Every farm in the valley comes through my door this month.
winter: Ice on the wheel. I chip it off every morning with a spoon. Don't laugh.
gangsters: Somebody's been using my back room to count something that isn't flour. I've stopped going in there.
penguins: The penguins love the mill. They slide down the flour chute when they think I'm not looking.

always: A warm room, a hot stew, and nobody asks your business. That's an inn.
Half the stories in {town} start at my fireside. The other half end there.
Sit, sit. You look like a person who's walked a long way.
rain: Rainy days are full-house days. Everyone wants a fire and a story.
winter: Hot cocoa, no charge, for anyone who shovelled the square.
gangsters: The back booth's yours, boss, any night. I keep it clear.
penguins: Big Jim came in for stew and ate the whole pot. Paid in fish. I'm not complaining.
festival: Festival nights, the inn never sleeps. Neither do I.

always: Drink water. Eat something green. Sleep. That's ninety percent of medicine.
If you get hurt out there, come straight here. Don't be brave about it.
I patch up farmers, miners, and once a very embarrassed goat.
spring: Spring sniffles season. Wash your hands.
summer: Sunburn. Every summer. Hats, people. Hats.
gangsters: I don't ask how anyone gets their bruises. I just fix them.
penguins: Coldy brought me a frostbitten pup. Carried it all the way down the mountain. She's softer than she looks.

always: Lovely day for it, whatever it is.
Good to see you around, {name}.
{town}'s a good place. Better with you in it.
rain: Wet one today. Good for the crops, at least.
winter: Cold enough to freeze your thoughts.
festival: Are you going to the plaza? Everyone's going.

always: Seeds by the door, prices on the shelf, gossip at the counter. The gossip's free.
If you're short on something, ask. I'll order it in, or tell you who's got it.
{name}! You look like someone who skipped breakfast. Again.
I keep a ledger of who owes me. I keep a smaller one of who I owe. Yours is in the small one.
spring: Spring seeds fly off the shelf. Turnips first, always turnips first.
summer: Corn and tomatoes, that's summer in a basket. Plant them before the 10th.
fall: Pumpkins! The whole valley wants pumpkins this month.
winter: Winter's quiet in here. Come in and warm your hands, even if you're not buying.
rain: Rain's good for the fields and bad for business. I'll take the trade.

always: Copper, iron, then the good stuff. Bring me bars and I'll make your tools sing.
A tool that fits your hand is worth two that don't. Swing it till it knows you.
The forge never really goes cold. Neither do I.
You hear that hum in the anvil? That's iron telling you it's ready.
winter: Best season for smithing. The forge keeps me warm and the work keeps me honest.
summer: Hot out, hotter in here. Don't touch anything orange.
rain: Rain on the roof, hammer on the anvil. Good rhythm, that.
gangsters: The President's men buy blades by the crate. I make them dull on purpose. Don't tell.

always: Potions don't brew themselves. Mostly. Some of them try.
Mind the green bottle. It's not dangerous, it's just shy.
If you bring me herbs from the forest, I'll teach you what they do.
I talk to my plants. The plants talk back. We're working on manners.
spring: Spring herbs are the strongest. Everything wants to grow.
fall: Mushroom season! The good ones and the very bad ones look alike, so ask me first.
rain: Rain days are brewing days. Everything steeps better when it's grey.

always: The town's growing, {name}. Some of that is your doing.
A mayor's job is mostly listening. And signing things. Mostly signing things.
If you ever want something built in town, the hall has the plans.
{town} was half empty when I took this job. Look at it now.
festival: Festival day! Best day of the season. Eat everything.
winter: Mind the ice on the plaza. I've asked for salt. I've asked twice.
penguins: The Star Crystal chose well. I'll deny I said that if the council asks.

always: Keep your head down and your boots clean, and people forget to look at you.
Everyone in this town owes someone. The trick is knowing who.
I've walked every road out of here. They all come back.
Coffee? No? Smart. It's terrible.
gangsters: The President's got eyes everywhere. Most of them are bored. Bored eyes miss things.
You're getting a name. That's good and bad. Mostly good.
rain: Rain washes out tracks. Good day to go somewhere you shouldn't.

always: Fish bite at dawn and dusk. In between they're just thinking about it.
Patience, {name}. The lake gives to the ones who wait.
Caught a carp this big yesterday. Let it go. It had a look about it.
Bait's half the battle. The other half is not falling in.
summer: Summer evenings, the trout come right up to the dock.
winter: Ice fishing's not for everyone. It's barely for me.
rain: Rain stirs the fish up. Grab your rod.

always: I'm painting the light on the lake. It changes every minute. It's rude, honestly.
Everyone has a colour. Yours is a sort of hopeful green.
If you find interesting stones, bring them by. I grind them for paint.
Art's just noticing things, slowly, on purpose.
fall: Fall is the only season that paints itself.
winter: Snow is hard to paint. It's all the colours pretending to be white.
rain: Rain makes everything shine. Best light all week.

always: Did you know the valley used to be a lake? The stones remember.
I've read nearly every book in the library twice. The third time is where it gets interesting.
Knowledge is a lamp, {name}. You don't hoard a lamp; you hold it up.
Ask me anything. If I don't know, I'll know someone dead who did.
winter: Long nights, long books. Winter's my season.
rain: Rain's for reading. I've got three going at once.
penguins: The old texts mention a falling star over this valley. Twice. Long ago, and now.

always: Water in the morning, before the sun gets greedy.
Every crop has its season. Plant out of season and it'll just sulk and die.
Good soil's half the work. Fertiliser's the other half. Talking to them doesn't hurt.
Need a hand? I've got two, and both have dirt on them.
spring: Spring rains do half the watering. Don't tell the sprinklers.
summer: Summer crops need water every single day. No excuses.
fall: Harvest what you can before winter. The frost doesn't negotiate.
winter: Winter's for planning next year. And for winter crops, if you're brave.

always: Flour on my nose? Probably. It's always there.
A warm loaf fixes most things. The rest needs two.
I bake at dawn. The whole street smells like bread by six.
If you bring me berries, I'll make you something you'll remember.
fall: Pumpkin pies all month. I've stopped counting.
winter: Spiced bread in winter. My gran's recipe. Secret ingredient: more spice.
festival: I've baked for the whole festival. My arms will never recover.

always: Quiet steps, {name}. The woods hear everything.
Wolves keep to the hills unless something drives them down. Lately, something has.
I hunt what I need and no more. The forest notices greed.
Tracks don't lie. People do. That's why I like tracks.
winter: Easy tracking in snow. Hard everything else.
fall: The deer are fat and nervous. So am I, come to think of it.

always: When I'm mayor, the fountain will be lemonade. Write that down.
I climbed the bell tower once. ONE time. Nobody lets me forget it.
I'm nine and three quarters. The quarters count.
Do you need an assistant? I'm very assisting.
festival: I'm in charge of the festival! Well. I'm in charge of the balloons. Some balloons.

always: I found a frog with spots! I named it Spots. It's a good name.
Mum says I can't keep frogs in the kitchen. She didn't say anything about the bathtub.
Frogs sing at night if it's warm. Have you heard them?
I'm going to be a frog scientist. Or a potion-maker. Or both, for frogs.
spring: Tadpoles in the pond! Hundreds! I counted to forty and then they moved.

always: My kite went over the lighthouse yesterday. Marlowe gave it back. Again.
I collect shells. This one's my best. Don't touch it, look with your eyes.
If you hold a shell to your ear you hear the sea. Or your ear. Nobody's sure.
The wind's good today. Good for kites, bad for hats.
summer: Summer wind is the best kite wind. Everyone knows that.

always: I press flowers in my diary. This one's from the meadow. Don't tell anyone it's my diary.
Some flowers only open at night. I've seen them. Mostly.
I'm writing down everything that happens in town. You're in it. Page twelve.
Daisies mean innocence. Dandelions mean I was bored.
spring: Spring is when the diary gets heavy. All the flowers.

always: Thirty years I kept that lamp. Mostly by myself.
Ships haven't come in a while. I'd light it anyway, if it had oil. Habit, or hope.
Storm or calm, the sea's always talking. You just have to sit long enough.
Gulls are terrible company and I'd miss them dreadfully.
rain: Weather like this, the lamp's the only thing that matters.

always: Stone's honest. You hit it right, it breaks right.
The quarry's deeper than it looks. Mind the edges.
Coal, copper, iron, stone, brick. If it's heavy, I sell it.
My golems are long gone. The old ones were here before the quarry.
winter: Cold stone splits easier. Silver lining.

always: These runes are older than the town. Older than the valley, maybe.
Every ruin is a sentence. I'm still learning the grammar.
The deeper you go, the older the stories get.
I came here for a week, four years ago.
penguins: The star that fell here didn't fall by accident. The ruins say it was sent.

always: The marsh keeps its own time. Don't rush it.
Mushrooms and moss, mud and mist. Everything I need.
Visitors are rare. Tea? It's mostly marsh. Mostly.
The frogs told me you were coming. They tell me everything.
rain: Rain? Out here we just call it Tuesday.

always: Sheep are smarter than people think. Not smart. Smarter.
The orchard's best in late summer. Come pick something.
Wool today, jumpers tomorrow. That's the whole business.
My dog does the real work. I just carry the snacks.
fall: Apple season! Pressing day soon. Bring a basket.
